title: Waldorf Salad
subtitle: Crisp apples, celery, walnuts, and grapes in a light mayonnaise dressing
excerpt: The classic American hotel salad: chunks of crisp eating apple, celery, and walnuts tossed in a light lemon mayonnaise with grapes. Refreshing, crunchy, and completely timeless.

recipe.sourceNotes: The Waldorf Salad was created at the Waldorf Hotel in New York City in 1896 by the maitre d'hotel Oscar Tschirky, known as Oscar of the Waldorf. The original salad contained only apple, celery, and mayonnaise: the walnuts were added in later editions of the recipe. The salad was an immediate success and spread internationally through the Waldorf's fame and through American culinary influence. The original Waldorf-Astoria recipe, published by Tschirky in 1896, is one of the first documented hotel recipes in American culinary history. The salad became so famous that it was satirised in a 1975 episode of the British sitcom Fawlty Towers, in which the character Manuel is repeatedly asked for a Waldorf Salad he has never heard of. The dish is best made with Cox, Braeburn, or another apple that holds its shape rather than dissolving.

content.text: Toss the apple with lemon juice as soon as it is cut: apple flesh browns fast in the air and a brown Waldorf is not worth serving. Use a tart eating apple that holds its shape. The dressing should be light: thin the mayonnaise with lemon juice and yoghurt so it coats rather than smothers the salad.

items.preparation: Cox or Braeburn; cored and cut into chunks; tossed in lemon juice

content.text: Stir the mayonnaise, yoghurt, and lemon juice together to make the dressing. Season with salt and pepper.
Combine the apple, celery, walnuts, and grapes in a bowl. Pour over the dressing and toss gently to coat everything. Taste and adjust the lemon and seasoning.
Serve immediately or within 30 minutes: the apple softens if it sits in the dressing for too long. Scatter with celery leaves if available.
